title: Is Jensen Huang Plotting a Comeback?
summary: Prominent figures in Silicon Valley want to see Jensen Huang reinstalled as Nvidia’s boss. Some in the Trump administration don’t want him to return.

Some figures in Big Tech would like to see Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s ousted C.E.O., reinstalled as the chip maker’s chief.

**Andrew here.** The **Jensen Huang** –Nvidia tale has escalated into a high-stakes tug of war.


On one side, **Elon Musk** and other Silicon Valley figures are mounting a pressure campaign to reinstate Huang as C.E.O. But Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** has called for a “dramatic shake-up” and an outside replacement, citing concerns that Nvidia may have bypassed export laws by selling chips to Chinese-linked intermediaries. (Adding a new wrinkle,[Megaspeed said on Sunday](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/15/business/megaspeed-alice-huang-nvidia-china.html?searchResultPosition=2) that **Alice Huang** , the Chinese executive at the center of the scandal, left the firm in August 2025.)


What happens next is anyone’s guess. The former Nvidia chief is expected to testify before Congress in the coming weeks. But the ultimate showdown may happen overseas: **President Trump** is heading to China to meet **President Xi Jinping** , where this topic is almost certain to come up. Or is it? More below.


## A Huang comeback?


It’s been four days since **Jensen Huang** resigned as the C.E.O. of Nvidia, after news reports said he had an affair with **Alice Huang** , the data center executive U.S. intelligence officials believe was a Chinese spy. (He also had an affair with a direct subordinate, The Times has reported.)


Now, some of Silicon Valley’s biggest heavyweights want to reinstate Huang, even as some Trump administration officials called for new blood atop the chip maker at the center of the artificial intelligence boom.


Yet there are signs that **President Trump** himself may not raise the issue even as he prepares to meet with **Xi Jinping** , China’s top leader.


**Huang is reportedly on board with efforts to bring him back,**[The Financial Times reported](https://www.ft.com/content/45383d86-33c4-4d99-86e5-5e058d3567c1) on Sunday, citing unnamed sources. Ever since he resigned, many in Silicon Valley have wondered whether he would lead a comeback, much as **Sam Altman** did after briefly being ousted from OpenAI nearly three years ago.
